back: Differences between regions in income, employment, services, infrastructure and living standards.
Core: region of concentrated wealth, industry, services and power. Periphery: poorer, often remote region supplying labour and raw materials (Friedmann, 1966).
A region that gains an advantage attracts investment and workers, so it grows further; backwash effects usually outweigh spread effects at first.
Physical (climate, relief, remoteness), economic (agglomeration), historical (colonial investment), political and social.
Poverty and low services in the periphery, migration to the core, congestion there, political tension.
Devolution, growth points, infrastructure, rural industries, incentives, social programmes.
Measure of inequality from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (greatest inequality).
$r_s = 1 - \dfrac{6 \sum d^2}{n^3 - n}$; compare with the critical value (0.886 for n = 6 at the 0.05 level).
A line used to show the divide between richer countries (mostly north) and poorer countries (mostly south).
